FR-016_durable_daemon_owned_intent.evidence: The browser submitted an idempotent request_ref through the real handler; the durable store kept one row across response loss and reload; only the private fixture advanced daemon-owned lifecycle state.

FR-017_truthful_status_and_release.evidence: HTTP 202 remained admission only. Status rendered submitted, queued, acknowledged, running, unavailable, failed, and completed distinctly. Completed status was accepted only after a different published readable View existed and common release returned its safe result metadata.

FR-018_authority_privacy_and_no_fallback.evidence: The browser received no workstation path, credential, daemon owner, environment, private locator, raw result identifier, or filesystem capability. The old pinned View remained stable; completion announced a released candidate and did not auto-repin or read the working copy.

FR-019_feature_boundary.evidence: S4 is accepted for the integrated candidate. Together with the already retained T032 S3 acceptance, this closes the implementation prerequisite for full Feature 011; it does not itself implement Book Context, release, deploy, publish, tag, or alter Working Agent Memory R1.

SC-007_online_offline_daemon_behavior.online: Durable submission progressed through acknowledgement, claim/execution representation, a new published View, and authorized common-release status readback before completed was shown.
SC-007_online_offline_daemon_behavior.offline: A separately controlled fixture remained queued or unavailable, exposed no result, and offered retry only from unavailable; HTTP acceptance and elapsed time never became completion.
SC-007_online_offline_daemon_behavior.separation: Online completion required explicit daemon-owned state transitions plus published readable View release. Offline state remained nonterminal. Neither path inferred the other, and no local/disk fallback was used.

SC-008_trigger_to_readback_trail.evidence: Browser action -> real authenticated HTTP request -> registered operator-code handler -> typed UCI IndexIntent/store operation -> durable row/status -> authorized released result readback was observed. Fixture-only lifecycle SQL stayed outside browser traffic.

recovery_and_rollback.response_loss: Reload reused the same request_ref and reconciled the existing intent; two admissions produced exactly one durable row and no duplicate execution identity.
recovery_and_rollback.terminal_new_work: An explicit same-kind action after failed created a different request_ref and one new durable row rather than replaying or mutating the failed intent.
recovery_and_rollback.retry: Retry was accepted only from unavailable and retained the original intent_ref.
recovery_and_rollback.rollback: Stop new browser admission or revert the HTTP/UI adapter while preserving durable intents, existing Views, source data, worktrees, and private UCI recovery state. No destructive cleanup is part of rollback.

prohibited_claims: No production daemon, production database, real working-copy mutation, secret, deployment, installation, tag, push, publication, or release was used or authorized.
The fixture-controlled daemon lifecycle is acceptance evidence for the bounded S4 contract, not proof of a production daemon installation or owner availability.
